newsitem.title: USA: Negotations heat up between UAW, Chrysler.
newsitem.headline: Negotations heat up between UAW, Chrysler.

text.p: Senior negotiators from the United Auto Workers union have moved their operations into Chrysler Corp's headquarters, a company spokeswoman said Sunday, while a union source said a new labor deal could be reached as early as today.
"We've been in pretty intensive negotiations at the subcommittee level for the last two days," said Nicole Solomon, a spokeswoman for Chrysler. "We believe we're making progress."

Solomon said it was unclear whether a new labor pact covering the 66,000 UAW workers at Chrysler could be reached Sunday. She said UAW President Stephen Yokich and Robert Eaton, chairman and chief executive officer of Chrysler, met Saturday afternoon. Other negotiators met past midnight Saturday.

A source close to the union said UAW officials are "optimistic" an agreement can be reached Sunday. The previous three-year agreement between the UAW and Detroit's Big Three automakers, which covers nearly 400,000 workers, expired September 14.

The UAW and Ford Motor Co reached a tentative agreement September 16 on a deal that calls for Ford to guarantee employment for 95 percent of its current 105,000 UAW workers over the life of the three-year pact. Final ratification by all of Ford's UAW locals is expected later Sunday.
The UAW extended the deadline for Chrysler and General Motors Corp. A new deadline has not been set, said Solomon.
